item.description:

In the longer term artificial intelligence could also lower prices by increasing productivity ​and making goods cheaper, she said.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV: In age of AI, the family is the first school of humanity
item.description:
# Pope Leo XIV: In age of AI, the family is the first school of humanity At the same time, the Holy Father underscored, the rapid development of artificial intelligence risks creating new forms of technological dependence, with poorer nations increasingly reliant on wealthier ones.
## The family as the first school of humanity With this in mind, he said that artificial intelligence "must never be allowed to erode this primary cell of society — whether by reducing persons and relationships to data and simulations, by flooding young minds with content that distorts desire, or by economic models that make family life economically precarious."
## Strengthen marriage and families "Dear friends, the world does not need an artificial intelligence that diminishes humanity; rather," Pope Leo insisted, "it needs human intelligence enlightened by wisdom, political authority guided by conscience and technological innovation directed by charity."
Only then, he said, will artificial intelligence become not a rival to humanity but a servant of the common good.
- [artificial intelligence](https://www.vaticannews.va/en/taglist.cultura-e-societa.Cultura.scienza.intelligenza-artificiale.html)

item.title: Artificial Intelligence Collides with FDA Bureaucracy: News Article
item.description:
# Artificial Intelligence Collides with FDA Bureaucracy A recent peer-reviewed [review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12455834/) of the field finds it already detects tumors on scans as accurately as radiologists, designs new antibiotics in weeks, tailors cancer treatment to a patient’s genome, and forecasts outbreaks before they crest. A separate look at some [200 studies](https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2025/08/22/hhs-artificial-intelligence-kennedy-fda/) in the journal Healthcare reached the same conclusion: used well, AI lowers costs and improves outcomes.
AI is no exception.
Telehealth and weight-loss companies use AI to tailor doses, flag complications, and guide patients in real time.

item.title: The Artificial Intelligence Arms Race: America Is Spending Billions, But China May Have Found a Cheaper Way to Win
item.description:
# The Artificial Intelligence Arms Race: America Is Spending Billions, But China May Have Found a Cheaper Way to Win ### Former JPMorgan Chase Global Chief Economist (Ph.D. in Economics) & Global Keynote Public Speaker for Hire The competition between the United States and China to build the world’s most capable artificial intelligence models has evolved from an American-led race into an effective two-horse contest.
For example, the latest [Kimi K3 model,](https://broadbandbreakfast.com/chinese-ai-model-takes-u-s-by-surprise-with-abilities-rivaling-claude-and-chatgpt/) developed by the Beijing-based startup Moonshot, has earned respect from the best versions of Anthropic’s Claude and OpenAI’s ChatGPT.
###### Source: [Artificial Analysis](https://www.google.com/url?sa=i&source=web&rct=j&url=https://tech-insider.org/llama-4-vs-qwen-vs-mistral-2026/&ved=2ahUKEwiekIvO9bOWAxUEq4kEHVxSKNAQy_kOegYIAAgHEAE&opi=89978449&cd&psig=AOvVaw2nVfirUtwSUFerUxoYTYms&ust=1787477200970000) The underlying philosophy is straightforward: if more computing power can produce better reasoning, greater reliability, and more capable AI agents, then build more computing power. This is an expensive strategy, but it allows American companies to keep pushing the technological ceiling.
DeepSeek’s sparse mixture-of-experts architecture exemplifies this philosophy. Rather than activating every parameter for every task, sparse models selectively use portions of the network.
This initiative seeks to upgrade China’s physical and digital infrastructure and spans six areas, including electricity, water, telecommunications, computing, logistics, and underground pipe networks.
###### Source: [Time Magazine](https://time.com/7358519/ai-china-us-race-graphs/) This has eased concerns about data sovereignty by giving companies greater control over their AI infrastructure at an affordable price.
That infrastructure provides an important foundation for training and deploying increasingly computationally intensive AI systems.
Stanford reports that China leads the United States in industrial robot installations.
At the same time, China is likely to focus on efficient models embedded in robotics, manufacturing, edge devices, and enterprise applications.
Meanwhile, China might lead as the primary source of affordable, open-weight, locally deployable AI, especially in manufacturing-heavy economies and parts of the Global South.
In the coming years, the key question may not be which nation creates the most advanced model, but which one successfully combines intelligence, cost-effectiveness, computing infrastructure, talent, and global reach.
